claims.claim_ar: التفات السرد إلى خطاب مباشر موجه إلى جماد/مخلوقات غير ناطقة (نداء الأرض والسماء)، أي تحويل الرواية إلى صيغة الأمر المباشر.
claims.claim_en: A shift to direct address (iltifat) addressed to inanimate/ non-speaking entities (the earth and the sky): the narrative turns into a direct imperative.
claims.needs_review_reason: The supporting source quote is an analogous tafsir example (Tabari) showing the pattern 'قيل + أمر' from a different verse rather than the exact ayah text in the provided chunks; the device attribution is inferred from that parallel.

claims.claim_ar: تكرار لفظة «وَقِيلَ» واستخدام التكرار مع النداء لتهويل الأمر وإبرازه، أي بديع (تكرار) يخدِم الغرض البلاغي.
claims.claim_en: Repetition (takrar) of the verb 'وَقِيلَ'—the repetition together with the vocative serves to intensify and dramatize the decree.

claims.claim_ar: اللفظ «بُعْدًا» أسلوب إنشائي/دعائي للدعاء بالهلاك على الظالمين؛ تعبير إنشائي يختصر الحكم والحكم بالهلاك.
claims.claim_en: The word 'بُعْدًا' functions as a performative exclamation/prayer for destruction (an insha'i utterance), expressing condemnation and final doom for the wrongdoers.

warnings: Not all provided tafsir chunks contain the exact ayah text; several claims are supported by analogous commentary passages (e.g., Tabari's 'قِيلَ لَهَا ادْخُلِي...') rather than a verbatim quote of S11:A44. Such parallels were used to justify the rhetorical readings.

Some rhetorical labels (e.g., 'iltifat') are inferred from analogous examples in the commentary rather than from an explicit statement in the chunk about this specific ayah; these inferences are marked with 'needs_review_reason'.

No direct chunk substring for the imperatives 'ابْلَعِي' / 'أَقْلِعِي' or other specific words of S11:A44 was available in the provided chunks, so devices tied to those individual word-forms were inferred at the ayah level or from parallel excerpts only.
